title: Towards Unified Surgical Scene Understanding:Bridging Reasoning and Grounding via MLLMs
summary: Surgical scene understanding is a cornerstone of computer-assisted intervention. While recent advances, particularly in surgical image segmentation, have driven progress, real-world clinical applications require a more holistic understanding that jointly captures procedural context, semantic reasoning, and precise visual grounding. However, existing approaches typically address these components in isolation, leading to fragmented representations and limited semantic consistency. To address this limitation, we propose SurgMLLM, a unified surgical scene understanding framework that bridges high-level reasoning and low-level visual grounding within a single model. Given surgical videos, SurgMLLM fine-tunes a multimodal large language model (MLLM) to support structured interpretability reasoning, which is used to jointly model phases, instrument-verb-target (IVT) triplets, and triplet-entity segmentation tokens. These tokens are then temporally aggregated and serve as prompts for a segmentation network, enabling accurate pixel-wise grounding of triplet instruments and targets. The entire framework is trained end-to-end with a unified objective that couples language-based reasoning supervision with visual grounding losses, promoting coherent cross-task learning and clinically consistent scene representations. To facilitate unified evaluation, we introduce CholecT45-Scene, extending CholecT45 dataset with 64,299 frames of pixel-level mask annotations for instruments and targets, aligned with existing triplet labels. Extensive experiments show that SurgMLLM significantly advances surgical scene understanding, improving the primary triplet recognition metric AP_IVT from 40.7% to 46.0% and consistently outperforming prior methods in phase recognition and segmentation. These results highlight the effectiveness of unified reasoning-and-grounding for reliable, context-aware surgical assistance.
tldr: This paper introduces SurgMLLM, a unified framework for surgical scene understanding that uses a multimodal large language model (MLLM) to jointly perform high-level reasoning (e.g., phase recognition, IVT triplet prediction) and low-level visual grounding (pixel-wise segmentation). It is trained end-to-end and evaluated on a newly extended dataset, showing improved performance.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了 SurgMLLM，一个用于手术场景理解的统一框架。它使用多模态大语言模型（MLLM）联合执行高级推理（如阶段识别、IVT三元组预测）和低级视觉定位（像素级分割），并进行端到端训练。在一个新扩展的数据集上评估，显示出更好的性能。
summary_zh: 手术场景理解是计算机辅助干预的基石。尽管近年来的进展（特别是手术图像分割领域）推动了该领域的发展，但实际临床应用需要更全面的理解能力——能够同时捕捉手术流程语境、语义推理及精确的视觉定位。然而，现有方法通常孤立处理这些组件，导致表征碎片化与语义一致性不足。为突破此局限，我们提出SurgMLLM——一个统一的手术场景理解框架，将高层推理与低层视觉定位融合于单一模型中。针对手术视频输入，SurgMLLM通过微调多模态大语言模型实现结构化可解释推理，同步建模手术阶段、器械-动词-目标三元组及三元组实体分割标记。这些标记经时序聚合后作为分割网络的提示信息，实现对三元组器械与目标的精确像素级定位。整个框架通过耦合语言推理监督与视觉定位损失的统一目标进行端到端训练，促进跨任务协同学习并生成临床一致的场景表征。为支持统一评估，我们构建了CholecT45-Scene数据集，在CholecT45基础上扩充了64,299帧器械与目标的像素级掩码标注，并与现有三元组标签对齐。大量实验表明，SurgMLLM显著推进了手术场景理解：核心三元组识别指标AP_IVT从40.7%提升至46.0%，在阶段识别与分割任务上均持续超越现有方法。这些成果验证了统一推理-定位框架对于实现可靠、情境感知手术辅助的有效性。

title: VoxCor: Training-Free Volumetric Features for Multimodal Voxel Correspondence
summary: Cross-modal 3D medical image analysis requires voxelwise representations that remain anatomically consistent across imaging contrasts, scanners, and acquisition protocols. Recent work has shown that frozen 2D Vision Transformer (ViT) foundation models can support such representations, but typical pipelines extract features along a single anatomical axis and adapt those features inside a registration solver for one image pair at a time, leaving complementary viewing directions unused and producing representations that do not transfer to new volumes. We introduce VoxCor, a training-free fit--transform method for reusable volumetric feature representations from frozen 2D ViT foundation models. During an offline fitting phase, VoxCor combines triplanar ViT inference with a compact closed-form weighted partial least squares (WPLS) projection that uses fitting-time voxel correspondences to select modality-stable anatomical directions in the triplanar feature space. At transform time, new volumes are mapped by triplanar ViT inference and linear projection alone, without fine-tuning or registration. Voxel correspondences can then be queried directly by nearest-neighbor search. We evaluate VoxCor on intra-subject Abdomen MR--CT and inter-subject HCP T2w--T1w tasks using deformable registration, voxelwise k-nearest-neighbor segmentation, and segmentation-center landmark localization. VoxCor improves the hardest cross-subject, cross-modality transfer settings, reduces encoder sensitivity for dense correspondence transfer, and yields registration performance competitive with handcrafted descriptors and learned 3D features. This positions VoxCor as a reusable feature layer for downstream multimodal analysis beyond pairwise registration. Code, configuration files, and implementation details are publicly available on GitHub at \href{https://github.com/guneytombak/VoxCor}{guneytombak/VoxCor}.
tldr: VoxCor is a training-free method that creates reusable volumetric features from frozen 2D Vision Transformers for establishing consistent voxel correspondences across different 3D medical imaging modalities (e.g., MR-CT). It combines triplanar feature extraction with a weighted partial least squares projection during a fitting phase, enabling direct nearest-neighbor search for correspondence at test time without fine-tuning or registration for each new volume pair.
tldr_zh: VoxCor 是一种免训练方法，利用冻结的 2D 视觉变换器生成可重用的体素特征，用于在不同 3D 医学成像模态（如 MR-CT）之间建立一致的体素对应关系。它在拟合阶段结合了三平面特征提取和加权偏最小二乘投影，从而在测试时无需针对每个新体对进行微调或配准，即可通过最近邻搜索直接查询体素对应关系。
summary_zh: 跨模态三维医学图像分析需要能够跨成像对比度、扫描设备和采集协议保持解剖结构一致性的体素级表征。现有研究表明，冻结的二维视觉Transformer（ViT）基础模型可支持此类表征，但典型流程仅沿单一解剖轴提取特征，并在配准求解器中针对单幅图像对进行特征适配，导致其他互补的观察方向未被利用，且生成的表征无法迁移至新体积数据。本文提出VoxCor——一种基于冻结二维ViT基础模型、无需训练即可生成可复用体积特征表征的拟合-变换方法。在离线拟合阶段，VoxCor将三平面ViT推理与紧凑的闭式加权偏最小二乘（WPLS）投影相结合，利用拟合阶段的体素对应关系在三平面特征空间中选择模态稳定的解剖方向。在变换阶段，新体积数据仅通过三平面ViT推理和线性投影完成映射，无需微调或配准操作。随后可通过最近邻搜索直接查询体素对应关系。我们在受试者腹部的MR-CT跨模态任务及跨受试者HCP的T2w-T1w任务上，通过可变形配准、体素级k近邻分割以及分割中心点定位进行评估。实验表明，VoxCor在最具挑战性的跨受试者、跨模态迁移场景中表现优异，降低了密集对应迁移的编码器敏感性，其配准性能可与手工描述符及学习型三维特征相媲美。这使VoxCor成为超越成对配准的下游多模态分析中可复用的特征层。代码、配置文件及实现细节已在GitHub开源：\href{https://github.com/guneytombak/VoxCor}{guneytombak/VoxCor}。
